title: The pipeline of workflows: every step behind a project's numbers, stale steps found, one step rerun from its record
request: Pipeline v1: the problem, data, analysis, solution workflow, evaluation and report as one object with lineage, resumable, its state on the graph; done when a project's pipeline lists every step that produced its numbers and reruns one step from its record. The main product stores it as a pipeline version's graph.
spec: A versioned contract of ordered steps with inputs, outputs, run and fingerprint; a builder from a project's records; staleness from what each run read; a rerun of one step as a job; routes; the main product's graph and digest.
plan: Read what the run records (19.5) and the replay already give.
Read the main product's pipeline version row and its digest at the pinned commit.
Write the contract, the builder and the rerun, then the routes.

decisions.decision: A step's staleness comes from comparing what its run recorded reading with the project now.
decisions.why: The run record already says what it read; nothing else needs to remember it.

decisions.decision: The graph sent to the main product holds what the pipeline is, never its state.
decisions.why: Its content digest would otherwise make a new version every time a stage runs.

decisions.decision: A rerun runs as a job.
decisions.why: A whole stage replayed inside a request would bypass the limits on jobs at once and Stop.

decisions.decision: The report's numbers are compared with what their runs made, not with the records read again.
decisions.why: Comparing a record with itself can never fail.

change: dclab_core/pipeline.py (new; dclab-core 0.28.0, contract pipeline.v1), dclab_core/adapters/main_product_pipeline.py (new) and main_product_fields.json, dclab_rnd/studio/pipeline.py (new), jobs/handlers.py (the rerun job), audit.py (a replay kind), agentic/routers/projects.py (two routes), the web client; tests/test_pipeline.py (new), test_experience_log.py; CHANGELOG, the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.defect: The report's numbers were said to differ from their records for numbers written inside text.
findings.scenario: 10 of 47 paths ending in @0 or @1 were compared as missing values.
findings.cause: A path walker of its own that did not read the n-th number of a text.
findings.fix: The report library's own context and lookup resolve every path.

findings.defect: The report check could be removed without any test failing.
findings.scenario: A planted fault returned no differences and every test passed.
findings.cause: No test made a report number differ.
findings.fix: A test alters one report number and expects it found.

findings.defect: The analysis step was missing and the contract could not name it.
findings.scenario: 6 of 53 report numbers, the findings of the training rows, were traced to no step.
findings.cause: The pipeline built the report without the analysis the product's report includes.
findings.fix: An analysis step of its own kind, its numbers the findings the report cites; the report depends on it.

findings.defect: The report rerun compared each record with itself and could never fail.
findings.scenario: A holdout value edited to 0.123 in the final record still gave the same report and a done stage.
findings.cause: Both sides were read from the same records moments apart.
findings.fix: Report numbers are compared with what their runs recorded when they ran; a record that no longer says what its run made makes its stage stale.

findings.defect: A stage's numbers written in text were credited to the whole chain through the report.
findings.scenario: 10 of 47 report numbers, such as a protocol text's first number, were said to come from the final stage and the report.
findings.cause: The report step held every path and was found first.
findings.fix: A number's step is found among the other steps first, then by its path's root with the suffix read off.

findings.defect: The main product's digest changed when a stage ran.
findings.scenario: The digest before and after running the stages differed though the pipeline had not changed.
findings.cause: Each node carried how its step is rerun, which depends on whether it has run.
findings.fix: The graph holds only what each step is and reads.

findings.defect: The steps sat on the wrong graph nodes and the pipeline's state reached no node.
findings.scenario: The solution was placed on the split design and the final stage on one of its two nodes.
findings.cause: Node ids guessed rather than read from the graph.
findings.fix: Steps carry the graph's own nodes (the final stage both of its two); the route gives each node the worst status of its steps.

findings.defect: A rerun ran a whole stage inside the request.
findings.scenario: Ten concurrent reruns of the model stage would run ten screens in the server's threads, past the limit on jobs at once, and a final replay left no audit row.
findings.cause: The route called the replay directly.
findings.fix: A rerun is a job of its own kind; a replayed final stage is written to the audit trail.

findings.defect: The lineage showed the rule's choice after a person chose another.
findings.scenario: An approval with another model left the step's output naming the rule's model.
findings.cause: The choice was read from the run, fixed when it ran.
findings.fix: The step shows the record's choice, the rule's beside it and whether it was overridden; an override is not taken for an edit.

findings.defect: A stage from before run records stayed done after its inputs changed.
findings.scenario: A setting changed on an old project left every old stage done.
findings.cause: With no run record there was nothing to compare and the stage was called done.
findings.fix: Such a stage is not recorded, and what read it cannot be vouched for.

findings.defect: Any key error inside a rerun answered that the step does not exist.
findings.scenario: A failure deep in the report build would return 404.
findings.cause: One exception handler wrapped the whole rerun.
findings.fix: The step is resolved first; only an unknown step answers 404.

measurements.name: the binary replica's pipeline
measurements.gate: every step listed with its run, every report number traced to a step, one stage replayed with the same numbers, the report matching what its runs made
measurements.result: 11 steps; 53 report numbers each traced to a step; the model stage replayed: 376 numbers compared, the same; the report: 53 numbers, 8 compared with their runs, none different
measurements.against_gate: every check holds on the replica
limits: One replica; only the numbers a run kept (its first ones) and the holdout value can be compared with runs.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test
measurements.result: 16 of 18 planted faults caught; the 2 left are equivalent changes (steps are ordered; the analysis lists its paths exactly)

outcome: A project's pipeline lists every step behind its numbers with its run, finds stale steps and where to resume, and reruns one step from its record as a job; the main product can store it as a pipeline version.
lessons: A check that compares a record with itself cannot fail: compare with what was fixed when the run happened.
A digest of a definition must hold only the definition, never state that changes as work runs.
Read the host's own node ids rather than guessing them.
risks: The graph page does not show stale steps yet.
Only a replay compares the code a run ran on.
The analysis is rebuilt with the report rather than recorded as a run.
